title: Cost snapshot inline-edit: undo affordance, playback prototype, and error-state handoff
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Goal: Design an inline-edit flow for Cost Snapshot tiles that supports fast edits to cost attribution tags, safe undo/redo affordances, and a playback prototype to demonstrate edit history for stakeholders. The work includes microcopy for error states, keyboard accessibility for inline actions, behavior during rollouts (canary vs global), and QA acceptance criteria for visual polish and edge cases. Rationale: product teams ask for a quicker way to correct misattributed cost tags without leaving the snapshot and for a clear way to revert accidental changes. This feature must degrade gracefully during canary rollouts and when the backend returns partial failures.

Scope: visual designs (high and low fidelity), interaction spec (keyboard + touch), animation frames (minimal fade/slide), error states (validation, backend conflict, network loss), undo affordance (ephemeral dismiss + full history playback), analytics hooks for usage, and a testing checklist for QA. Not in scope: backend implementation, API contract changes (tracked in ENG-8243), or billing recalculation logic beyond triggering a refresh.

Trade-offs considered: 1) local optimistic updates with ephemeral undo vs server-confirmed commit: chosen approach is optimistic UI with a 7-second ephemeral snackbar allowing undo, followed by commit and addition to persistent edit history. This balances perceived speed and recoverability. 2) Inline edit complexity vs modal approach: we keep edits inline for power users but fall back to a modal for multi-field edits. 3) Animation subtlety vs performance: minimal motion to reduce repaint cost on heavy dashboards.

Stakeholders: Product (Ravi Patel), Console PM (Leah Morgan), Engineering lead (Anika Shah), Observability (Kai Tran).
acceptance_criteria: Inline edit affordance appears on hover/focus for cost snapshot tiles
Edits apply optimistically with a 7-second undo snackbar visible
Playback UI exposes a chronological history of edits with timestamps and actor
Error states: validation and conflict errors show clear microcopy and suggested actions
Keyboard accessibility: Tab/Enter/Escape flows work for edit, save, cancel, and undo
Canary rollout behavior: when in canary, edits show a non-blocking banner explaining limited persistence
QA visual polish checklist passed: spacing, contrast, motion thresholds, and responsive layouts
Telemetry events emitted for edit_start, edit_commit, edit_undo, edit_error, and playback_open

Contrast check: banners and inline labels meet AA standard
Rollout test: simulate canary user flag and ensure banner explains limited persistence
Playback: open edit history, confirm timestamps and actor initials, and verify revert from history
